test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 24 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The marked price of a revolving chair is ₹15,000. It is available on two successive discounts of 20% and 12%. What is its selling price (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price can be calculated directly by applying successive discount percentage multipliers to the Marked Price.

SP = MP × (100 − D₁)% × (100 − D₂)%

SP = 15000 × 80% × 88%

SP = 15000 × 0.80 × 0.88 = 12000 × 0.88 = 10560

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,560.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹15,000

First discount (D₁) = 20%

Second discount (D₂) = 12%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − D₁)/100 × (100 − D₂)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c81daa4268f832ed4aa1a0de75308f41aa03ff7c9cd989d1b1470168407bcab4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 15000 × (100 − 20)/100 × (100 − 12)/100

⇒ SP = 15000 × (80/100) × (88/100)

⇒ SP = 15000 × 4/5 × 22/25

⇒ SP = 15000 × 88/125

⇒ SP = 120 × 88

⇒ SP = 10560

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,560.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Successive Discount

When two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂% are given, the equivalent single discount percentage can be calculated directly using the formula: [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100]%.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

A discount is always offered on the Marked Price (MP) of an item. The price obtained after deducting the discount is the final Selling Price (SP). The fundamental formula connects them as SP = MP − Discount.

Relation between CP and MP

If a profit of P% is made by a shopkeeper even after allowing a discount of D%, then the direct ratio between the Cost Price (CP) and the Marked Price (MP) is given by CP/MP = (100 − D)/(100 + P).
